Couldn't tell ya .... but hopefully someone here can.

• The sub-compact P320 is quite a bit taller than the G26, 4.70" vs 4.17" both because of the larger magazine (12 vs 10 rounds) and because of the higher bore axis. You can get a 12 round factory mag for the G26.

  • Barrel length is longer at 3.6" vs 3.4".

  • On the Glock, you can change trigger reach with a backstrap swap, with the P320, you have to swap the entire frame and there's fewer options because of this.

  • The trigger does not have the center safety tab.

  • The takedown lever juts out more than the G26.

  • Magazine removal for malfunction drills is a little different, designed to be gripped on the sides.

  • Trigger guard is rounded on the P320 subcompact and square on the G26, which makes it a little less likely to snag when holstering and not possible to rest your off-hand index finger on the front, if you're in the small minority who does so.

  • Stock sights are metal and tritium.

  • Slide stop is further rearward and juts out more.

  • You can buy different barrel lengths, slides, and frames without additional FFL checks because the legal "firearm" is just the removable trigger assy.

My guess as to why they chose the P320:

  • They want a high production volume striker-fired polymer pistol. That leaves Glock, M&P, XD, P320.

  • They want an American company with American manufacture. That leaves the M&P and the P320.

  • The P320 doesn't have the goofy trigger, is more modular, and doesn't have a removable backstrap because that's just one more thing for the grunts to screw up.
